pages:
VISITOR LOG, Signal Test 7 week. Passes
stay at the desk.
Nobody goes past the white line alone.

A cast of the Line 1 forehead crystal,
made for the funding visit.
The real one is still in him.

Bed 3 is for staff. Line 1 handlers keep
reporting the same headache.
Logged as "the hum".
Restorer unit, set to gentle.

Someone has glued a cover over the
overdrive switch.

SIGNAL TEST 7. Output: 140 percent.
Crest crystal stress: red. HOLD.
Handwriting on the screen frame:

"Do not run Test 8. Not on him."
- C. Finch

Lines 2 to 9: asleep. Lights low after
eight.
They dream when the core runs loud.
AMBER LINE. Kept for study, never woken.

This week, three of them turned to face
the door.
The feeding schedule has been torn down.

Under it, in marker: WE ARE LETTING THEM
OUT.

Vat 3 drained Tuesday. Whoever was in it
went down to the river.
Nobody signed for it.

Core load: OVERDRIVEN. The helix hums
the same note as the Line 1 crest.
It is getting louder.
From here you can see the river.

The Breakout is tonight. Leave every
door open behind you.

The last room. Corvin has been waiting
all day.

Take your time. Nobody rushes the last
fight.

I climbed all eight floors just to watch
this one.
No pressure. Well. Some pressure.

battle_won:
Washed out at the first wave.
It's fine. The sea doesn't gloat.

Lights out, superstar.
The crowd still cheered for you.

pages:
The stairs to the next room are open.
Keep climbing.

The Arena staff patch your team up. Full
health, all of them.

Courtesy of the house. Ron is waiting
down in the lobby.

A cream envelope. Heavy paper. Your name
written by hand.

"Dear {player}, and dear {lead}. We hope
the soup was warm."

"And that the bins went out. We are so
proud of you both."

"Thank you for everything you have done
for them."

"There is a disturbance on Wellspire, at
the top of the old river."

"We think it would like to see you.
Nothing bad will come of it."
"Take a coat. With love, Head Office."

No signature. No employee number. Just
that.

A postcard, too. A snowy peak on the
front.

"Snowed in up north. All fine. Teo says
hello."

"Marta says the benches here are a 3."
- the field team

The Skylift High Line at Frostspire is
running again.

And the old riverbed north of
Brookhollow is dry enough to walk.

SKYLIFT HIGH LINE. Service resumed at
Head Office's request.
Have a lovely trip.

"HIGH LINE: SERVICE SUSPENDED."
The sign is thick with dust.

A field team clipboard hangs on the
gate.

Eight team names signed in. None signed
out.
Every one of them is home.
A survey peg, RT blue. The tag reads:

"Cloudway. Surveyed by RT, year of the
founding."

Under it, newer pencil: "This path was
not here this morning."
Stones are stacked into a little cairn.

One for each person who has climbed
past.

You count them. You quit counting at
your own age.

Writing scratched into the cave wall,
old and careful:
"EVERY ONE OF THEM CAME OUT OF A LAB."
"WE REMEMBER. WE WERE NOT MAD."

Under it, smaller: "don't let it in your
head"
A field notebook left on a ledge.

Every page has the same entry, in
slightly different handwriting:

"Subject arrived. Subject climbed.
Subject went up."

"Subject came back down. Subject does
not remember."

A weather board, frozen. The forecast
for tomorrow is chalked in already:
"Same as today."

An RT staff locker. Inside: a field team
jacket your size.
The name patch has been unpicked.

Wren: RT Hydrology, Team Cobalt. You
too?

Wren: This river has been dry for three
hundred years.

Wren: Our maps say there is no river.
Our maps say there is no mountain.
Wren: Show me what you've got.
Wren: I keep measuring the riverbed.

Wren: It keeps being a little deeper
than yesterday.

Ansel: Field Researcher, Cobalt. Head
Office sent us a letter.

Ansel: Handwritten. No signature. Did
yours smell of snow too?

Petra: Field Lead, Cobalt. Eleven years
on the northern survey.

Petra: Never once seen this valley. I
don't trust places that show up.

Petra: Let's see if you're real, at
least.

Petra: Keep going up. Everyone does, it
seems.

Joss: RT Survey Pilot. I flew over this
range on Tuesday.

Joss: Clouds the whole way. Flat ground
under them.

Joss: Then I took the lift, and here we
are.

Ilse: Harrow. Do you get the feeling
you've climbed this before?
Ilse: Every step, half a second early?

Ilse: There. You did the thing with your
foot before the loose rock.
Ilse: Like you knew.

Odo: Team Gannet, geology. This rock is
old. Very old.

Odo: And it isn't on a single core
sample we own.

Odo: Maybe the samples are wrong. Maybe
the rock is.
Odo: I keep both in the same bag.

Maren: Gannet. Someone at Head Office
said "it would like to see you."

Maren: It. Not they. I've been thinking
about that word all day.

Maren: Sorry. Nerves. The mountain hums
when you stand still.

Maren: Some of the hum sounds like my
own thoughts.

Tobin: Field Lead, Gannet. We filed a
report that this region doesn't exist.
Tobin: Head Office stamped it "noted".
Tobin: Just "noted". Then they sent you.
Sela: Harrow. Last one before the ice.

Sela: I'm meant to halt anyone who isn't
ready.
Sela: Nobody told me who decides that.

Nils: Team Sedge, ice cores. The ice
here has a layer for every winter.

Nils: Thousands of them. And they're all
the same winter.

Hedda: Sedge. You're the one from
Brookhollow?
Hedda: You came through here in spring.

Hedda: ...Didn't you? I have a photo.
It's blurry.

Rook: Field Lead, Sedge. Our radio picks
up a signal up here.

Rook: It's RT's old call sign. The one
from before the rebellion.
Rook: Nobody's used it in a lifetime.
Fenna: Weather Watcher, Team Lark.

Fenna: The clouds up here don't move
with the wind. They move with you.
Fenna: Walk left. See?

Fenna: My barometer reads "fine", with a
little picture of a sun.
Fenna: It never had a picture.

Fenna: Up here you keep your thoughts
tidy.

Fenna: Head Office says don't let it in
your head.
Fenna: Never said what "it" was.

Dov: Either way, the plates know your
weight.

Dov: They shifted before your foot came
down.

Linnea: Field Lead, Lark. We're here to
observe the disturbance.

Linnea: Funny thing. The disturbance
arrived when you did.

Ezra: Sound Recordist, Team Quill. Clap
once.

Ezra: ...The cave answers twice. The
second one is a little bit late.
Ezra: Like a memory.

Gus: Cartographer, Team Moraine. I've
drawn this ridge four times today.
Gus: Every map comes out different.

Gus: Except the bit where you're
standing. That's always the same.

Hal: Field Lead, Moraine. They warned us
about the top.

Hal: Not what's there. Just "don't look
straight at it."

Hal: Who's "they"? Good question. The
memo was signed by us.

Ione: Senior Researcher, Team Vesper.
We've been waiting.
Ione: Longer than you'd think.

Ione: You always come up the cave on the
left. Today you came up the left.
Ione: Good.

Corwin: Vesper. I keep a list of things
I remember that never took place.
Corwin: You're on it. Twice.

Agathe: Field Director, Vesper. Head
Office asked me for one thing.

Agathe: Watch the field researcher
closely.

Agathe: I asked which researcher. They
said "the one who is watching."
Agathe: Let's begin.
Agathe: The summit is just above.

Agathe: Whatever you see there, write it
down before you blink.

The light flings you back to the top
landing.
Your team is healed. Try again.

Phase 3: Own colour. Its crystal
flickers river blue.
The dream's tune comes back.

Free. Still screaming the cracked
signal.

It turns on you. Not hate. The pain,
looking for somewhere to go.

Dawn. Ondravel carries you down the
river to a wide bend.

Boats are coming. It lies down in the
bend and stays.
It already knows this is how it goes.
It nudges you back toward the light.
River blue fades. The present.

The same dome, the same Ondravel. It has
waited fifty years for you.

The old crystal crumbles from the
inside. It steps out.

Every crystal stays on and keeps
working.
But the throb in the violet is gone.

Up at the summit, the dry spring
trickles.
Ondravel bows to {lead}, not to you,

and goes down the old riverbed toward
home.

A river bank in a storm. The river is
full,
higher than any mark you have seen.

Violet light throbs like a heartbeat.
Your team flinches, then steadies.

Lantern Rest. The field team walks in
with you from the mountain road.

All of them. Ron is already there with
the keeper.

Coralie: I knew your face the minute you
walked in.

Coralie: I couldn't say. You hadn't done
it yet.

Night shift log, Lab 1. "Enclosure
stable. Subject calm. All doors sealed."
"Visitor: one. Signed in by: nobody."

"Field jacket, about your height. Looked
like they'd been here before."
The clouds tear open from the middle.
Light comes down like a staircase.

At the bottom, taller than the spire, is
Ondravel.

You have the strangest feeling that he
is surprised you are on time.

Keeper: The old rebellion stories have a
kid in them. Field jacket.

Keeper: Walked into Lab 1 and let the
light out.

Keeper: My gran told it to me when I was
small.

Keeper: Funny. The kid looked a lot like
you.

Teo: The readings from the summit came
back. Flat.

Teo: Nothing has been up there for
centuries.

Teo: ...Then why does everyone in
Cairnfold remember the light?

Down in the lowland towns, the RT field
teams wake up at home, one by one.

There is mountain dust and ice-melt on
their boots by the door.

Each of them has a blank letter in a
coat pocket.

Every clock in their houses quit at the
same minute.

Nobody can say where the last few weeks
went.

"Must have been a long shift," somebody
says. Somebody always says that.

Far to the north, past the old riverbed,
something folds quietly away.
Nobody looks up.
Dawn. You wake up in your own bed.

The crystal on the shelf glows the way
it always does.
The violet throb is gone from it.

Your boots by the bed are dusty with
something pale,
like ice-melt dried in the sun.

By the bridge, a thin trickle runs in
the dry riverbed.
Nobody seems to notice.

In the mud, one big wet print, heading
downstream.

RITA's report form is already open on
the front desk.

Title: your ID number. The body of it is
blank.
Through to the field team room.

Teo, Marta, Pell and Imke are at their
desks as if they never left.

The kettle is on. There is mountain dust
on their boots.

You open your mouth to tell them where
you've been...

On Teo's desk is a list. "Find source"
is crossed off,
in a hand he doesn't seem to recognise.

You can't remember what you came in to
say. It doesn't seem important.

Tech: Visitors aren't on tonight's
sheet.
Tech: Pass? No pass. Right.

Tech: The ring on the floor was humming
all night.
Tech: It went quiet when you came in.

The lab, long ago. Rows of tanks glow in
the dark.
Small shapes turn over inside them.

Staff in white coats write on
clipboards.

A light flashes over each tank, and the
shape inside it flinches.

Many small lights press against a glass
dome. You are not in it.

Bryn, Team Lark: The wind died the
second we got here.
Bryn: Nobody trusts it.

Otto, Team Harrow: Three teams, one
fire.

Otto: First time we have all agreed on
anything.

Sunniva, Team Quill: I keep recording
the spire.

Sunniva: The tape comes back with a hum
on it.

Lorcan, Team Moraine: My map ends at
this camp.

Lorcan: Past here, the lines will not
stay put.
Crates stamped RT FIELD STORES.

Rope, cocoa, spare batteries. Someone
packed for a long stay.

A small weather mast. The needle points
at the spire,
whichever way the wind blows.
